cnn.title: Abusers convicted in Joanne Young case echoing Pelicot
cnn.desc:
In the first trial of its kind in England, four men have been convicted of raping and sexually abusing a British woman, in a harrowing case that bears similarities to that of Gisèle Pelicot in France. Like Pelicot, Joanne Young chose to allow her name to be made public, after discovering that her then-husband had advertised her online to strangers for sex, repeatedly drugged her and raped her. British police sought the expertise of French investigators on the Pelicot case to assist them in bringing Young's former husband and her other abusers to justice.Also: AI tech giant Anthropic becomes one of the world's most valuable public companies after its stock market debut. Meanwhile Meta says it is ''re-evaluating'' its 2030 climate goals as the demand for AI data centres drives up emissions. A spacecraft that has been on an eight year journey through outer space is set to enter orbit around Mercury. We hear the Ukrainian view on the face-to-face meeting between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s largest religion by 2035. We meet the winner of the International Children's Peace Prize, 17-year-old Colombian climate activist Francisco Vera Manzanares. And who are the candidates challenging Fifa President Gianni Infantino for the top job in world football? The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: UN court says Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingyas
cnn.desc:
The International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority. It's the first such ruling against a state by the court. The ICJ rejected Myanmar’s argument that it had responded to insurgent attacks.Also: the presidents of China, the US and Russia stress the importance of stable energy flows, UN reform and the prevention of nuclear proliferation at a trilateral summit, internet access is cut in South Korean exam halls, amid fears of cheating. And a remarkable discovery reveals that 125,000 years ago hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert. The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: BBC reports from Ukraine's undergound frontier
cnn.desc:
We go inside the old Soviet-era gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia. The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the tunnels where this subterranean battle is taking place. Also: the AI giant Anthropic is set to raise more than 80 billion dollars in its initial public offering, breaking a record set by SpaceX. President Trump pushes back against global regulation of ''Super Intelligence'' - or AI - at the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of his meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. The US defence secretary Pete Hegseth signs a military cooperation deal with America's former foe Venezuela. Democrats in the US House of Representatives nominate Hakeem Jeffries as first African American Speaker. A new study suggests a pill that mimics Viagra can slow cognitive decline in people with Alzheimer’s disease by almost a third. Rare footage from Brazil shows about 20 Indigenous men and boys emerging from their self-imposed isolation deep in the Amazon rainforest. And a painting by Vincent Van Gogh sells at auction in New York for over 190 million dollars - a record for work by the artist. cnn.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
cnn.desc:
President Trump was greeted by President Xi Jinping at the airport as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting on Thursday between the pair and the Russian president. In a highly choreographed moment, Trump and Xi shook hands on the tarmac. Later the US leader met Mr Putin ahead of a gala dinner. Also: Thousands of people in Haiti have marched in the capital in support of troops from El Salvador, who've been deployed to confront the island's powerful criminal gangs. The Democrats have taken Alaska from the Republicans in the final senate race of the US midterms, nearly three weeks after election day. We hear from a former child refugee from South Sudan, who has walked the entire length of the UK to draw attention to the war in Sudan. And - after more than 13 years, GTA 6 - the latest instalment of the multi billion dollar video game franchise is released amid huge fanfare and expectation.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Nvidia rules out return for disgraced boss
cnn.desc:
Jensen Huang fails in his bid to be re-hired as CEO of Nvidia after a scandal over his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The US Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating whether the company misled investors. Nvidia has meanwhile reported a doubling of revenues during his last quarter in charge.Also: President Donald Trump is attending a regional economic summit in China, a day ahead of a historic meeting with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, and the Russian leader, Vladimir Putin, in the city of Shenzhen. The US has lost its measles-free status and infections are continuing to spread. Researchers have been learning more about humpback whales by using drones to collect their snot. We have a report from the West Bank after a 72-year-old Palestinian woman was shot dead by armed settlers in Jericho. New research has found that genes inherited from Neanderthals can reduce the risk of schizophrenia. A Georgia O'Keefe painting that was hidden in a cupboard for years has sold at auction for 4.8 million dollars. And the spacecraft Voyager 1 will clock up a milestone - reaching a distance of one light day from earth.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Special episode: Trump, Putin and Xi meeting
cnn.desc:
This special episode of the Global News Podcast brings together our China specialist, our North America correspondent, and our Russia and Ukraine analyst, to discuss an unprecedented summit taking place this week.
The US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet in Shenzhen, China, for their first-ever trilateral talks. President Trump has said the agenda will include denuclearisation, the war with Iran, and the war in Ukraine. So what could emerge from this meeting? Some analysts are hopeful that China could exert some influence on Tehran, and act as a mediator between Moscow and Kyiv. But Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he's worried that the three leaders could try to reshape the international order as they see fit, without consulting smaller countries. Trump, Putin and Xi are also expected to talk about the economy and AI, particularly after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO of Nvidia, following allegations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But will any big decisions come out of the talks in Shenzhen? Or is this about symbolism: a way for the leaders of China, the US and Russia to give themselves a boost and a distraction from their problems at home? cnn.title: OpenAI sued by California over rogue cyber attacks
cnn.desc:
The California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI, alleging the ChatGPT maker misled the public and put people at risk by developing AI models without adequate safeguards. The lawsuit cites the July 2026 attack on the AI platform Hugging Face, in which experimental OpenAI agents accessed the internet and breached the company's internal systems. An OpenAI spokesperson told the BBC that the lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab".Also: Five European countries have announced plans to set up immigration "return hubs" in Rwanda. Robert Pattinson has been named as the new James Bond.  Russia and Ukraine have launched major attacks on each other, destroying three key bridges. A forensic expert has told the BBC he believes Jeffrey Epstein's death was the result of a homicide, not suicide. And controversy in South Africa over the removal of wild baboons from Cape Town.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.desc:
The Russian defence ministry says a record number of drones were fired from Ukraine overnight and more than 1300 were brought down by its air defences. An oil refinery in the Krasnodar region was targeted and there was damage to the Kerch Bridge which links Russia to occupied Crimea. Western countries call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza. The Indonesian president apologises to neighbouring countries for the thick haze caused by massive forest fires in his country. The director of the Shakespeare Institute threatens to resign if plans to move the centre from Stratford-upon-Avon to Birmingham go ahead. cnn.title: Government forces retreat in Yemen
cnn.desc:
Yemen's Saudi-backed government has been redeploying its forces to protect its temporary capital, Aden, after advances by the Houthi movement which is backed by Iran. They've withdrawn from an area overlooking the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait at the entrance to the Red Sea. It signalled the end of a six-week counter offensive to retake coastal territory from the Houthis, whose control over the Yemeni side of the Strait has further constrained Middle East oil exports. Also: the architect of Mexico's cocaine trade Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies at the age of 80. Guatemala declares 30-day state of emergency amid drug trafficking violence in the eastern districts of Zacapa and Izabal. WHO research published in Lancet Global Health finds one in four teenagers worldwide has not been physically active for at least 60 minutes on any day in the previous week. Taliban authorities ban cricket on Kandahar radio. Prince Harry praises war veterans on surprise visit to Ukraine. Canadian Stephanie Case becomes the first woman to complete the Antarctic Ice Ultra Marathon. cnn.title: The Global Story: How North Korea pulled off a $6bn heist
cnn.desc: Last week saw what could be the biggest heist in history: $6.3bn was stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. North Korean hackers are suspected of being behind the attack, which saw billions of dollars disappear in just 20 minutes. It’s far from the first time North Korea has been accused of a major cyber-attack. Over the past decade, hackers linked to the country have targeted banks, public institutions and even Sony Pictures. On The Global Story, Asma Khalid speaks with journalist Geoff White, host of the BBC investigative podcast The Lazarus Heist. He explains how this isolated country become a major player in the world of cyber-crime – and where all that money goes. The Global Story brings clarity to politics, business and foreign policy in a time of connection and disruption. For more episodes, just search 'The Global Story' wherever you get your BBC Podcasts.

cnn.title: SpaceX makes history catching part of returning spacecraft
cnn.desc:
Part of SpaceX's Starship rocket was caught as it descended back to Earth in Texas. It's the first time the upper section of a reusable rocket has ever been captured. Mechanical arms carried out a "chopstick" manoeuvre to catch the spacecraft. The breakthrough could dramatically cut the cost of space travel and marks a major step towards making Starship suitable for human spaceflight.Also: Ukraine's president says the US has, for the first time, floated the idea of Ukraine joining NATO in exchange for ceding control of the Donbas region to Russia. We hear from the first black senator of the US state of Mississippi in 145 years. A fierce debate is brewing in Germany over the future of Hitler's Eagle's Nest after the building was destroyed by fire. A leading specialist in detecting digitally manipulated images warns that deepfakes are becoming almost impossible to spot. And a Philippine teenager has won the first-ever Eurovision Asia competition.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens.
